reason: The Select a budget placeholder on the enabled budget picker measures 2.61:1 (#9d9da8 on #fbfcfd, 15px) on both sampled states, where AA needs 4.5:1. A visible label (Reimburse from, Budget) names the control, so the text is not essential, and 2.61 is above the 2:1 line for high: it stays medium.

Tab skips Expense because the selected segment has tabindex -1 and Mileage is the only tab stop. Enter on Mileage selects it, then Expense becomes the tab stop and takes focus on Shift+Tab, so no function is out of keyboard reach. Separate from this claim: the tree exposes button Expense with no selected state, a 4.1.2 problem worth its own finding.
criterionAnalysis: 2.1.1 Keyboard: every function of the Expense/Mileage control works from the keyboard. Activating the selected segment only re-selects the current value, and the other segment is reachable and operable with Tab and Enter; after the switch the roles of the two segments swap. 2.1.2 No Keyboard Trap and 2.4.3 Focus Order: focus enters and leaves the control in a sensible order. 4.1.2 is a different claim from this finding (the selected state is not exposed) and is not what the sweep flagged here.
